results.title: Pashupatinath Temple, Kathmandu, Nepal
results.text: This is a very good temple of Lord Shiva. It is spread in huge area. Apart from main temple, there are many small temples inside the campus. It is being told that Bhim ( one of the Pandavas in Mahabharat) wanted to worship Lord Shiva and he was searching Lord Shiva in Himalays. To take test of Bhim's devotion and to hide from Bhim, Lord Shiva hided himself in the look of a buffalo. But, Bhim identified Lord Shiva even in the form of buffalo. Then, Lord Shiva (in the form of buffalo) tried to hide himself by going beneath the ground(land). But, Bhim caught tail of buffalo. The place where Bhim caught the tail is presently known as Kedarnath (one of chardhams of Hindus) and Shiv linga in Kedarnath(India) is rear part of buffalo and the front part (face side) is in Pashupatinath, Kathmandu, Nepal.The shiv linga in Pashupatinath is having four faces of shiva on four sides of shiv linga(East, west,north and south). The devotee must perform Darshana of all four faces. There are many brahmins available in temple . Devotees can perform "Pujavidhi" through them with nominal charge @ Rs.311/- . Overall it was very good experience.

results.title: Educational, Moving & Inspiring
results.text: Located 30 minutes from the heart of Kathmandu is this Hindu spiritual temple(s) & cremation site. It can be very confronting for people who have not seen an open air cremation on a funeral pyre, let alone 10 in a row all burning simultaneously. It is sombre and reflective, yet also a fascinating step-by-step peak into the Hindu culture and tradition of cremation and and celebration of life. As you walk through the grounds you are exposed to every aspect of this process and as unusual as it may sound, photography is welcome, common and in some cases encouraged. There are many iconic Sadhu's (holy men) lounging in hidden nooks and prayer areas in the buildings surrounding the pyres, they come complete with their long dreadlocks & glazed eyes, particularly the younger ones. Take a little time to do a thorough walk-thru if you're chasing a photograph of an older 'wise' Sadhu, if you look closely and explore the myriad of mini temples and surrounding buildings, you are bound to see some extremely photogenic locals! These amazing characters won't talk but many will pose for photos and welcome the opportunity if a few Rupees are on offer. (Always show respect and ask first or point at your camera and nod, watching for their reaction) There is also a cornea depository bank just behind the main cremation area, it is the very last stop in a long list of processes and rituals. The spiritual river trickling through the grounds and separating it into two distinct sides is the iconic Bagmati. This section flows very slowly during much of the year and with all of the activities on the banks and never-ending dumping of ashes, it is nothing short of putrid and foul. It remains however, a highly recommended spot to pay a visit to while in Kathmandu. You will leave with a deep appreciation for the fascinating and ancient processes that occur in religions around the World.  It is one of the most significant Hindu temples of Lord Shiva in the world that is open to the public. (**note: a few specific areas are off limits to women and non-Hindus- signage is posted**) Allow for 2 hours. Entry fee in effect. Taxi from Thamel = 25 minutes.

results.title: Hard to explain one's feelings
results.text:
This is a very surreal experience.  It is difficult to process the experience in Western norms.  American grieving process is very antiseptic.  This is (in our experience) a very strange process.  The river where ashes are distributed is considered holy, but to the observer is horribly polluted, complete with trash, livestock wandering and dogs.  Bodies are cremated on pyres located above the river and ashes spread into the river below.  Families of the deceased gather with the body next to the river prior to cremation.  There is a building located next to the temple that functions like what we would consider a hospice.  When a person is deemed terminal and near death, they are brought to this place to die at a holy site.  

It is a place to be respected and one needs to be cognizant of this and act accordingly.  You will be set upon by very aggressive folks trying to sell items on the way in and out.  They will follow you relentlessly until you finally reach your ride to leave.

I would recommend this to anyone visiting Kathmandu, but be prepared for an experience the likes of which you have never seen before.

results.title: Inspiring
results.text: Entering Pashupatinath is an inspiring experience. It is a sacred place, where cremations take place. You can just feel the atmosphere and looking at the ceremonies is an amazing experience. I would like to point out that you are looking at funerals, so be respectful of people, I think you do not want that people come and go, and take pictures of your dears' funeral.

results.title: Solemn and exciting but overpriced!
results.text: We went to discover this holy Hindu temple with its historical details but not allow to enter as it's reserve for Hindu unfortunately. Instead, we were assigned to watch a funeral service of hindu rites at the opposite stand. Though we never seen one before which could 'excite' ones, it should be a private affair and respect the departed , not expose to the public. Worse still we have to pay double for entrance fee (was up after its new year day). This is like stealing from the dead and am sure they can rest in peace!

results.title: Shiva temple
results.text: The most important divine place in Kathmandu. Entry fee is high (NRs 1,000/-) but worthy place to see the Hindu traditions in practice in a single place. Sadly, non-Hindus are not permitted here.

results.title: 1000 NRs - Really?
results.text: It was a rip-off at 250 NRs. I don't mind supporting tourist attractions, but there is a limit. Everybody else walked in for free. They stopped us (westerners) to extract an entrance fee (apparently needed to pay for all the fee collectors). The site has not benefited noticeably from the fees and generally offers little to see.
